candidates.evaluation_plan: Re-run the deterministic methods or compatible baselines on the extended benchmark. Compare standard aggregate scores with per-slice scores, measure whether limitation-focused slices expose performance drops not visible in aggregate results, and report reproducibility across repeated deterministic runs.
candidates.expected_contribution: A reproducible benchmark add-on that turns broad future-work limitations into measurable evaluation slices for deterministic methods.
candidates.gap_statement: The evidence cards consistently indicate deterministic methods with benchmark evaluations and experiment signals, while also noting that each paper highlights an unspecified limitation for future work. This leaves a gap: the current benchmark signals may not isolate which conditions trigger the reported limitations.
candidates.hypothesis: If benchmark cases are organized around explicit limitation-triggering conditions, then deterministic methods can be compared more diagnostically than with aggregate benchmark results alone.
candidates.proposed_method: Construct a stress-test benchmark extension that starts from the existing benchmark-evaluation settings reported across the papers, groups test cases by suspected limitation type, and reports per-condition experiment signals alongside standard aggregate metrics. The method would preserve deterministic evaluation protocols while adding structured failure slices and reproducible analysis templates.
risks: The provided evidence does not specify the actual limitations, so the first version may require manual extraction from the full papers.
Stress slices may be too narrow if the original benchmark tasks are not sufficiently diverse.
Per-slice findings may be hard to compare across papers if their benchmark settings differ substantially.
candidates.title: Limitation-Targeted Stress Benchmark for Deterministic Methods

candidates.evaluation_plan: Evaluate the base deterministic method and the wrapped version on the original benchmark plus a limitation-focused subset. Report changes in benchmark performance, flagged-case accuracy or error rate, abstention or fallback frequency, and deterministic reproducibility across repeated runs.
candidates.expected_contribution: A reproducible robustness layer for deterministic methods that operationalizes future-work limitations as detectable conditions and controlled fallback behavior.
candidates.gap_statement: Multiple papers describe deterministic methods and report experiment signals, but the evidence cards also state that each approach has a limitation left for future work. A natural gap is that deterministic pipelines may lack mechanisms for detecting when their own assumptions are no longer appropriate.
candidates.hypothesis: Adding an explicit limitation detector and fallback policy to a deterministic method can improve robustness on cases associated with known weaknesses while retaining reproducibility on standard cases.
candidates.proposed_method: Design a wrapper around a deterministic method that monitors predefined experiment signals, flags inputs or intermediate states associated with the known limitation, and routes those cases to an alternate deterministic subroutine, abstention path, or human-review queue. The core method remains deterministic, but its execution path becomes condition-aware.
risks: Because the evidence cards do not identify the specific limitations, detector design depends on further paper-level review.
Fallback policies may reduce coverage or increase computational cost.
If experiment signals are weakly correlated with failure modes, the wrapper may over-flag or under-flag cases.
candidates.title: Hybrid Deterministic Pipeline with Adaptive Limitation Handling

candidates.evaluation_plan: Assess the template by coding the included papers, measuring inter-annotator agreement for extracted fields, counting how often limitations and future-work clues can be mapped to measurable benchmark conditions, and surveying whether the template improves reproducibility planning for new experiments.
candidates.expected_contribution: A practical evidence-capture framework that converts high-level statements about deterministic methods, benchmarks, experiment signals, and future work into comparable research-planning artifacts.
candidates.gap_statement: The evidence cards mention benchmark evaluations, experiment signals, limitations, and future-work directions across several deterministic-method papers, but the metadata is too coarse to compare the limitations or signals directly. This suggests a reporting gap rather than only a modeling gap.
candidates.hypothesis: A standardized reporting template for deterministic-method experiments will make limitations, benchmark conditions, and experiment signals easier to compare and reuse in follow-on work.
candidates.proposed_method: Create a structured reporting framework that requires authors to document deterministic assumptions, benchmark setup, experiment signals, observed limitation cases, and proposed future-work targets. Apply the template retrospectively to the provided papers and use the resulting matrix to identify recurring evaluation gaps and missing diagnostics.
risks: The current evidence cards provide only abstract-level snippets, so full-text access may be required for reliable coding.
A template may be perceived as administrative unless it clearly improves reproducibility or follow-on evaluation.
Different benchmark domains may require domain-specific extensions to the common fields.
candidates.title: Cross-Paper Reporting Template for Deterministic Benchmark Signals
